reportedExperience.value: Home root heart beside a flame crossing; direct gate counters led to sealed H5 and a northern bypass.
An eastern four-cell loop reached the initial aim, but protecting it alone meant typed upkeep. I chose a larger sheltered southern territory preserving amber cherished northern cells.
I taught J4 a missing north passage with root reinforcement from J5, then closed its actual history. Contact cells became a boundary.
Autonomous amber roots cut the earlier crossing. The old causeway became a sealed memorial; lower F7/G7/H7 crossing renewed living home connection.
A new I6/I7/J6/J7 heart lived behind the boundary. Amber recovered detached K3. Closing F5 against a real announced attack completed coexistence.

Actual history was a useful construction ingredient: deliberate reinforcement taught the needed direction, and scars acquired a different strategic role. Losing the first route made the lower bridge and replacement heart matter.
Single-beat type counters often had an obvious winner. Final closed-edge counterplans repeated without adaptation, creating a quiet endpoint but no further meaningful challenge.

account.intention: Initial eastern bridge and home circuit attained. Larger ambition: preserve both lineages living hearts, keep a small connected eastern enclave, and turn the central contact scar into a stable coexistence boundary.
account.source: The visible counterpart has a cherished four-cell northern circuit; direct conquest would erase the most distinctive relation. The sealed H5 gate suggested a boundary made from actual contested history.
account.meaningfulResponse: Amber began direct typed counters at H4 and now I3; changing to a bypass beat local gate countering.
account.oldCreationNewRole: H5 changed from crossing gate to sealed boundary monument. B3 home loop persists while causeway supplies eastern reach.
account.uncertaintySkill: Need learn whether a border can remain quiet without constant type counters; exact single beat types and closed historical directions matter.
account.routineBurden: Already appreciable state reading and type switching; no finite stock bookkeeping.
account.nextActFor: Protect I4 enclave from announced shell and investigate closing only frontier contact edges without cutting its western connection.

account.intention: A stable north boundary and a southern living bridge preserving amber heart. The first eastern loop was opened to gain room; it must be renewed in the sheltered south.
account.source: Concrete contact history now makes a coexistence project possible, but simple sealing severs living connections as well as attacks.
account.meaningfulResponse: Amber countered from multiple border sources, including water. A G6 autonomous root changed the old causeway G5 into amber, then G4 too; old traffic matters beyond the announced action.
account.oldCreationNewRole: The first H5 gate and I4/J4 frontier are now boundary memorials, not active routes. Original home causeway is threatened; F7/G7 became a second crossing.
account.uncertaintySkill: Typed arrival plus placement on water remains tricky; I incorrectly expected flame at water G4 to stay flame, but it became shell and won ground flame G5. Single-action previews are useful, not recipe guessing.
account.routineBurden: Individual counter commands are beginning to resemble upkeep, but border construction gives them an architectural purpose.
account.nextActFor: Complete actual connected southern living space, check whether quiet coexistence is possible; do not pad to the diagnostic target after that purpose closes.

account.closure: Stop after the substantive coexistence project and its bounded stability trial, far below the mandated long target. Continuing to 180 would be unsupported padding or a newly manufactured conquest.
account.intention: Preserve the achieved world: home heart, connected sheltered eastern heart, and amber northern cherished heart coexist.
account.source: After the initial goal at 10, the larger project renewed purpose until the new eastern circuit closed at 35. Old road threat at 39 supplied one further real response at 40.
account.meaningfulResponse: Amber recaptured the intentionally detached K3 outpost at 36. After the F5 seal at 40 it entered an observed four-action cycle: J3 shell south, G5 flame east, H3 shell south, G5 shell west. Each strikes an already closed edge. The same cycle repeated twice with no ownership, history-contact count or reach changes.
account.oldCreationNewRole: The original flame causeway became a protected western memorial rather than the active route. H5 gate and H4/I4/J4/K4 contact cells became the coexistence border. F7/G7/H7 is now the living bridge. First eastern four-cell loop was sacrificed and renewed at I6/I7/J6/J7.
account.uncertaintySkill: Meaningful learning: memory closure needs the intended actual heading, and arriving root reinforcement can teach that history while defending. Terrain transformations and autonomous lingering fronts caused mistakes; exact previews resolved two specific actions.
account.routineBurden: The final eight waits confirmed a repeating blocked policy, not eight interesting decisions. Many earlier typed counters had a clear winning answer. Desire for peaceful structure carried the primitive work, but the game did not renew larger purposes after closure.
account.strongestStretch: Actions 20 through 24: teach the missing northward passage to an old contact cell, then use its actual history to make a boundary without taking cherished cells. Actions 27 through 35: old route lost, lower crossing and sheltered heart created.
account.weakestStretch: Final repeated blocked counterplans, plus local type counter upkeep without a larger architectural change.
account.nextActFor: Finish the world. This is not evidence that the 180 to 240 target sustained meaningful purpose, and is not a claim about human enjoyment.

account.endpointVerification: Public final view confirms an active amber northern circuit G1 south to G2 east to H2 north to H1 west to G1, with an amber tip at H1. The cherished I2/I3/J2/J3 footprint remains amber, but amber itself changed I3 and J3 to southward paths, so I do not claim the original exact cherished four-cell cycle stayed alive. Both lineages retain living circuits; preserved cherished ownership and preserved exact original route are distinct.

noticedResponses.value: Formed and remembered I2/I3/J2/J3 early; repeatedly countered local blue types from different sources; autonomous water root captured G5 then G4; recaptured K3 after I intentionally left it detached. Final post-seal policy repeated J3 shell south, G5 flame east, H3 shell south, G5 shell west twice into closed edges. No later ownership or contact changes occurred.

closure.value: Renewed beyond the first aim through a valued coexistence architecture, then exhausted. No basis to claim sustained 180-decision purpose or human enjoyment.

value.reason: A coherent larger coexistence project closed by 35; one old-road protection response at 40 finished it. Twelve total waits included a final eight-beat test showing the same ineffective four-action counterplan cycle twice. More play would be padding, conquest without motive or manufactured damage.

priorDesignerProposal: After freezing inspectable laws, run an actual mandated long diagnostic and a separate elective-interest condition; permit early stopping, retain identities and test changing roles rather than a turn quota.
limits: AI report and elective behavior do not establish human enjoyment.
Narrative/aesthetic value is recorded as a player account; no mechanical frontier can verify it.
No overall enjoyment verdict follows from passing the safeguards. The independent critic must inspect the proposed and observed experience.
